blocks.text: The integrated plan (P) is the strongest choice for this season in the model, within the available plan options.

It has the highest modeled crop production of the compared plans while keeping the lowest-field service share at the same level as today’s fixed-roster plan. It involves leveling fields, building two farm ponds, and repairing a shared watercourse; approvals and participant costs need to be confirmed.

blocks.text: No field is worse off than the fixed-roster baseline, but tail fields receive a smaller share of their allowance than head fields.

In the integrated plan (P), compared with today’s fixed-roster plan (B0), the equity check finds no fields with lower modeled production. The lowest service shares are concentrated in the tail and middle: A-010 is lowest overall, followed by middle fields A-004, A-031 and A-005, then tail field A-008; each listed field has a positive production change versus B0.

Allowance shares rely on assumed water rights, and production is modeled rather than measured. “Fair” here means the tool’s receipt-versus-allowance and baseline comparison, not a complete judgment of household fairness.

turns.message: Where does all the canal water actually go?

blocks.text: In the integrated plan, most canal water reaches field outlets; some is lost in channels, and some is stored briefly in ponds.

For the typical-weather, nominal-supply case, the canal withdrawal is split between water lost along channels and water arriving at field outlets. Of the outlet water, most goes straight to fields; a smaller amount fills ponds, which later release water and also lose some to evaporation and seepage. Groundwater also contributes to field application, so not all water applied to crops is canal water.

blocks.title: Water flow in the plan
blocks.caption: Follow the flows from the canal source through channel losses and field outlets to direct use and pond storage.
notes: source withdrawal = conveyance loss + outlet receipt (within float tolerance); soil-water and network/pond accounting are separate; ET components are not summed as losses
